entries.claim: The workflow guard regex-matches the raw YAML bytes, not the parsed values GitHub Actions evaluates. A YAML double-quoted escape (\uXXXX, \xXX, or an escaped line break) spells `secrets` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in a form none of SECRETS, MODEL_KEY or EVAL match, so a workflow can hand a step a model key and the test still passes.
entries.failure_scenario: Put this in .github/workflows/test.yml under a step: `env:` then `"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "${{ secrets.MODEL_KEY }}"`. PyYAML (YAML 1.1/1.2 semantics, the same ones the Actions loader uses) parses it to {'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY': '${{ secrets.MODEL_KEY }}'}, so the runner exports the repository secret as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. I ran the test's three regexes over the raw file and got zero matches each, so workflowProblems returns [] and 'no workflow runs the eval suite or sees a model key' passes. `run: "claude plugin eval ."` slips past EVAL the same way. The comment at line 109 shows the guard is meant to stop a command being hidden by YAML syntax (folded blocks), but it handles only one YAML transformation. The fix is to match against the YAML-decoded scalars, or to fail on any backslash escape inside a double-quoted scalar.
